Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa Top Swiss court upholds landmark Liberia war crimes ruling Source : Reuters 2 November 2026 2:05am Audio By Carbonatix
The top Swiss court on Friday confirmed a ​guilty verdict against a Liberian warlord, ‌upholding his 20-year sentence in the country's first-ever war crimes trial.
Alieu Kosiah, who ​fought in the 1990s against ​then-president Charles Taylor's army during Liberia's ⁠brutal civil war, was originally sentenced to ​20 years in prison in June 2021 ​for rape, murder and cannibalism.
An earlier appeal was rejected in 2023 by the Federal Criminal Court ​and the dismissal of his second ​appeal by Switzerland's highest tribunal the Federal Supreme Court ‌published ⁠on Friday closes the case.
"This is a landmark decision, made possible by the courage of these victims, who have ​written a ​page ⁠of legal history," said Alain Werner, Director of Civitas Maxima, ​an NGO representing victims in ​this ⁠case.
However, the court reversed a parallel conviction for crimes against humanity on the grounds that the 2011 law on this crime cannot be applied retroactively.
